data.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED empirically at ALL THREE sites, through the real emit() path.

Two-clone harness (bare remote + clones A/B sharing one tickets branch, base padded to the retention bound, both clones taken offline, one automatic emit each):
- pre-prune CONTROL merge: rc=0 every run
- plan_review/sidecar.py:89  -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
- code_review/sidecar.py:147 -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
- completion_sidecar.py:59   -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
Conflict text shows the shared base file 'renamed to' a DIFFERENT new UUID in each clone - the delete(oldest)+add(new-uuid) pairing that git rename detection resolves as a rename conflict.

Contract violated: docs/concurrency.md invariant I1 - convergence is 'never by deleting a committed event (I1 append-only)'. Prior art: bug 8185 / commit be8a0c059 removed the same mechanism from enrich_drain and overlap/digest_sidecar and explicitly spawned this ticket for the three siblings.

IMPORTANT nuance for anyone re-testing: rename detection is content-similarity based and rebar events are single-line minified JSON, so a one-byte length difference between the pruned and the new event can drop similarity below git's 50%% threshold and the merge spuriously succeeds. Build the base from a REAL emitted payload (equal-length neighbour) or the repro looks green. This is why the wedge appears intermittent in production and is then permanent.

FIX: removed the automatic prune() call from all three emit() paths (net -3 executable lines + docs). prune() itself is KEPT, importable and behaviourally unchanged, as an EXPLICIT operator-invoked operation - existing direct-call tests still pass untouched. Growth bound is a deliberately deferred tradeoff; merge-safe bounded retention is tracked as 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d.

Two pre-existing tests in tests/unit/test_audit_retention_cap.py asserted the DEFECT (test_code_review_emit_calls_prune: 'emit must prune the target ticket after appending'; test_code_review_emit_retains_the_cap: emit->prune wiring caps at 50). Both were added by story fde0, which introduced the automatic code-review prune this bug removes. They were INVERTED in place (not deleted) to pin the append-only invariant where the defect used to be, following the fix-out -> revise -> verify RED -> fix-in ordering.

SIBLING SWEEP (clean): every remaining delete_events call now sits inside an explicit operator-invoked prune(); zero automatic invocations remain in src/rebar. purge_bridge.py is the operator 'rebar purge-bridge' command.

NOTE on the AWS lead: the available AWS account holds an unrelated project (no instances in 17 regions, review-bot host not reachable), so NO production corroboration was obtained. The conclusion rests on the local two-clone experiment plus 8185's closed-bug record.
